current.text: He is the backup center behind Donovan Clingan. The experts do not expect him to start over Clingan.
He re-signed with Portland for 3 years and 44 million USD.
The contract shows the team trusts him. He outplayed Clingan in the playoffs.
He is expected to be capped at 17 to 18 minutes and to sit about 16 back-to-backs.
He is not draftable in 12-team leagues as a backup. He is a stash with top 60ish upside if Clingan gets hurt and Williams stays healthy.
At 23 minutes a night he would be a draftable category-league player.
His 2P% jumped to 74 last season, and an expert expects it to drop to about 68. Twos drive most of his FG% value.
Portland plays 10 games in our playoff weeks with a March 28 end, a weak schedule. The team has 15 back-to-backs, 3 of them in the fantasy playoffs.

durable.text: He is a shot-blocker with an elite FG%. Blocks are his standout category.
His free throw percentage swings wildly from season to season.
He has a long injury history. His minutes and health are hard to trust.
He makes almost no threes and scores few points, even for a center.

note: Both Yahoo and ESPN value him at 0 USD, and his ranks of 192 and 166 put him outside our 144-player draft. Leave him on waivers. His appeal is about 1.6 blocks and a near 70% FG% in limited minutes, which fits a punt PTS or punt 3PM big-man build. Early in the season, watch Clingan's health and whether Williams gets past the 17 to 18 minute cap. If either happens, spend FAB on him quickly.
